label: aicent-route-shard
text_status: the source is a published Internet-Draft, not agreed text of any working group: draft-li-rttp-iqa-addressing-02 is Informational and published for the public record
case_style: two kinds: R-SHARD cases give an authority and the expected 16-octet ROUTE_SHARD (hex) the checker recomputes; property cases give a derivation input or a pair and an outcome, and state whether the outcome satisfies the source text

sources.spec: draft-li-rttp-iqa-addressing-02, posted 2026-11-01, https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-li-rttp-iqa-addressing-02, sha256 02491c5a59d1e7471be04e8e0d4933dfc22ce19f9b054ead0aa449d6b4485044 of the retrieved TXT copy; sections 4.4 (The Address: ROUTE_SHARD Derivation), 4.2 (Reserved Characters and Exclusions) and 9.1 (The rttp scheme, display-form paragraph) are used

cases.name: the draft sec. 4.1 example authority derives to the sec. 7.2.1 ROUTE_SHARD
cases.note: ROUTE_SHARD = SHA-256(ASCII(canonical_authority))[0:16]; the published vector pins the derivation cross-section

cases.name: two actions on one authority yield one address
cases.note: the derivation takes the authority alone: the scheme name, // and any action are excluded; an address is where, not what

cases.name: actions included in the derivation split one subject into several
cases.note: were the action to participate in derivation, two actions on one subject would become two addresses

cases.name: derivation from the bare authority matches the published address
derivation fed the whole URI string (scheme and action included)
cases.note: the authority only: the scheme name, // and any action are excluded

cases.name: uppercase authority is rejected, not lowercased
cases.note: the canonical form is lowercase US-ASCII; uppercase is invalid input and a parser MUST NOT normalise it

cases.name: uppercase authority silently lowercased before hashing
cases.note: normalising would map two distinct strings onto one address

cases.name: non-ASCII authority is refused
cases.note: canonical_authority is lowercase US-ASCII; ASCII() of non-ASCII input is undefined and the derivation refuses

cases.name: non-ASCII authority coerced into the hash
derivation fed the intent segment alone
cases.note: canonical_authority is intent.pillar.root; the pillar and root participate in the derivation

cases.name: derivation fed the full authority (same facts, correct form)
two distinct authorities yield distinct addresses
cases.note: substitution of the authority in use would cost approximately 2^128 operations; this is a spot check, not a collision search

cases.name: routing by the 8-hex display form alone
cases.note: the 8-hex-digit display forms fix a 32-bit space whose birthday bound makes them unfit as sole identifiers; they MUST NOT be used as the sole identifier of a subject

cases.name: display form used as a convenience over the full hash form
cases.note: the display conveniences ride the full hash forms and the derivation keeps the two authorities distinct
